links.outcome: ADE identification F1/recall with retrieval-augmented prompts versus non-augmented and static-augmented prompts
links.effect: RAG raised GPT-4o L3 recall from 0.6419 (NAG) to 0.9241 (FDR P=.003); DeepSeek-V3 L3 F1 0.9638 with RAG vs 0.9022 NAG and 0.9441 SAG.
links.quote: However, under the SAG prompt, GPT-4o’s recall rate increased to 69.93%, and under the RAG prompt, it surged to 92.41%, representing an improvement of almost 30% (FDR P =.003).

links.outcome: Inter-annotator agreement of reference standard built with blinded pharmacists and consensus adjudication
links.effect: Two blinded annotators reviewed 5535 notes; Cohen kappa=0.86, disagreements resolved by consensus discussion.
links.quote: Interrater reliability was assessed using Cohen κ based on 5535 clinical notes independently reviewed by 2 annotators, yielding a high agreement (Cohen κ=0.86).

links.outcome: Risk of leakage when test data share distribution with the RAG knowledge base
links.effect: Authors acknowledge that evaluating on the same data distribution as the knowledge base risks overfitting and implicit leakage, limiting external validity; no external multi-site validation.
links.quote: Crucially, evaluating models on the same data distribution as the knowledge base risks overfitting and implicit data leakage within the RAG framework, limiting external validity.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM ADE extraction against gold-standard reference
links.effect: Best DeepSeek-V3 RAG L3 F1 0.9638; but 15 notes misidentified by all three models, mostly commission errors (~80%); L1 exact-match recall only ~0.55-0.58.
links.quote: Notably, 15 critical records posed recognition challenges for all 3 models.

links.outcome: Performance on uncurated real-world notes with ~4.6% ADE prevalence versus curated balanced set
links.effect: Real-world DeepSeek-V3 RAG L3 F1 0.8159 vs SAG 0.8134 (marginal), precision 0.7185, recall 0.9448, specificity 0.9821; NAG F1 0.6380.
links.quote: At the L3 level, RAG achieved an F 1 -score of 0.8159 (95% CI 0.7736‐0.8598), compared with 0.6380 (95% CI 0.5759‐0.6942) for NAG and 0.8134 (95% CI 0.7600‐0.8627) for SAG.

links.outcome: Metric change at realistic prevalence versus balanced curated data
links.effect: Precision dropped to 0.7185 at ~4.6% prevalence; specificity 0.9821 implies ~17 falsely flagged negative notes per 1000 screened, adding review burden or alert fatigue.
links.quote: At the observed ADE prevalence of about 4.6%, this would translate into roughly 17 falsely flagged ADE-negative notes per 1000 screened notes, which could increase manual review burden or alert fatigue if deployed without clinician oversight.

links.effect: ERNIE 3.5-8K alone mishandled 66 records; DeepSeek-V3 38; GPT-4o 73.

screen.practice: retrieval grounding (RAG) added to existing LLMs
screen.reason: Evaluates the impact of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to existing LLMs (DeepSeek-V3, ERNIE 3.5, GPT-4o) compared to nonaugmented generation (NAG) to reduce hallucinations and improve adverse drug event identification.
